html:
The Acts of Union of 1800 joined the Kingdom of Ireland to Great Britain to form the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, from 1 January 1801. The Irish parliament in Dublin was abolished.

After the rebellion of 1798, the British prime minister William Pitt wanted Ireland under direct control. Members of the Irish parliament were won over with peerages, offices and money. Pitt also meant to grant Catholics full rights, but the king refused.

Irish MPs now sat in London. The fight to repeal the union and win Catholic rights shaped Irish politics for the next century, from Daniel O'Connell to the Home Rule movement. The union lasted until the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921, and Northern Ireland is still in the United Kingdom.
sum: The Acts of Union of 1800 joined the Kingdom of Ireland to Great Britain to form the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, from 1 January 1801. The Irish parliament in Dublin was abolished.
